extracted.intended_audience: Hospitals, clinicians, post-acute care providers, and other stakeholders participating in or commenting on the proposed CJR-X episode-based Medicare payment model
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts evaluation and operational criteria from the proposed CJR-X (Lower Extremity Joint Replacement) episode-based payment model, including episode definitions, included/excluded services, duration and termination rules, and proposed quality measures tied to payment. Intended for implementers and commenters on the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode Initiation (anchor MS-DRGs and HCPCS; start date rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a beneficiary meets the beneficiary inclusion criteria at § 512.620, an LEJR episode would begin when a beneficiary is admitted for an anchor hospitalization for one of the following MS-DRGs or an anchor procedure indicated by one of the following HCPCS codes on an outpatient claim (hospital institutional claim billed through the OPPS): MS-DRGs 469, 470, 521, 522; HCPCS 27447 (Total knee arthroplasty), 27130 (Total hip arthroplasty). The episode start date would be the day of the anchor procedure for outpatient procedures and the date of admission for an inpatient hospitalization. However, if an anchor hospitalization is initiated on the same day as or within 3 days of an outpatient LEJR procedure, the episode would begin on the date of the outpatient procedure rather than the date of the inpatient admission. Transfers between hospitals follow CJR/TEAM alignment: a transfer from a CJR-X hospital in an included MS-DRG does not initiate a new anchor hospitalization; a transfer from a non-CJR-X hospital into a CJR-X hospital discharged under an included MS-DRG would initiate the episode at the receiving (second) hospital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the specific MS-DRGs and anchor HCPCS codes proposed. Explains precedence rules when outpatient procedure and inpatient admission occur close in time (within 3 days). Provides alignment with CJR Model and TEAM on transfers and when a second hospitalization initiates an episode. CMS seeks comment on proposal at § 512.630(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Items and Services Included in the Episode
rubrics_metrics.description: Include in the episode all items and services paid under Medicare Part A and Part B during the performance period, unless such items and services fall under a proposed exclusion. Include all Part A services furnished during the 90-day post-discharge period of the episode, other than certain excluded hospital readmissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes inclusion of items and services that are directly related to LEJR episodes or the quality and safety of care furnished during the episode (e.g., surgical wound infection). Example (non-exhaustive) list: physicians' services; inpatient hospital services (IPPS operating and capital payments); inpatient psychiatric facility services; Long-Term Care Hospital services; Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility services; Skilled Nursing Facility services; Home Health Agency services; Hospital outpatient services; Outpatient therapy services; Clinical laboratory services; Durable medical equipment; Part B drugs and biologics except those excluded under § 512.625(c); Hospice services; Part B professional claims dated in the 3 days prior to an anchor hospitalization if surgical procedure was performed outpatient but patient later admitted. Rationale: inclusive episodes incentivize coordination, avoid fragmentation of financial accountability, and align incentives for managing transitions of care, post-acute utilization, and complication-related services. CMS seeks comment on the inclusion list at § 512.625(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded Items and Services — diagnosis-category and MDC exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude from episodes all Part A and B items and services for hospital admissions and readmissions for specific categories of diagnoses (clinically unrelated to LEJR), determined by MS-DRGs, and exclude certain Major Diagnostic Categories (MDC) such as MDC 02 (Eye), MDC 14 (Pregnancy/Childbirth/Puerperium), MDC 15 (Newborns), MDC 25 (HIV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions apply to baseline and performance-year episodes. Rationale aligns with prior CJR/TEAM exclusions and aims to remove clinically unrelated admission/readmission spending (e.g., oncology, trauma medical admissions, organ transplant, ventricular shunts). CMS will post complete lists of excluded MS-DRGs for readmissions on the CJR-X web page and seeks comment on these exclusions (§ 512.625(c),(d),(e)). Revisions to exclusion lists would be initiated through notice and comment rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded Items and Services — IPPS new technology add-on payments (value code 77)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude IPPS new technology add-on payments for drugs, technologies, and services identified by value code 77 on IPPS hospital claims for episodes in the baseline period and performance years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New technology add-on payments reimburse specific new drugs/technologies/services that substantially improve diagnosis/treatment and would be inadequately paid under MS-DRG. Excluding them reduces potential for CJR-X to diminish beneficiary access or burden hospitals with counting these unpredictable/additional payments toward episode spending. Aligns with prior CJR Model exclusions (80 FR 73303–73304, 73315).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded Items and Services — OPPS transitional pass-through payments (status indicator H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude OPPS transitional pass-through payments for medical devices identified through OPPS status indicator H for episodes in baseline and performance years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These technologies have substantial cost but lead to substantial clinical improvement; exclusion is consistent with CJR Model final exclusions policy (80 FR 73308 and 73315).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded Items and Services — hemophilia clotting factors (IPPS and Part B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude hemophilia clotting factors (§ 412.115) identified through HCPCS code, diagnosis code, and revenue center on IPPS claims for baseline and performance years, and exclude outpatient/carrier/DME Part B payments for hemophilia clotting factors billed on those claims (including HCPCS codes with clotting factor = 1 and new hemophilia clotting factors not in the baseline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hemophilia clotting factors are costly and paid separately; CMS does not believe including them yields spending efficiencies. Specific HCPCS identification approaches described; CMS will update lists and post them on the CJR-X web page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded Items and Services — Part B high-cost and low-volume drugs (baseline-period criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: For episodes included during the baseline period, exclude drug/biologic HCPCS codes that: (1) are billed in fewer than 31 episodes in total across all CJR-X baseline episodes; (2) are billed in at least 31 episodes in baseline and have a mean allowed cost > $25,000 per episode in the baseline period; and (3) HCPCS codes corresponding to clotting factors for hemophilia identified in the quarterly ASP file or new hemophilia clotting factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: high-cost/low-volume items are essential to appropriate care of certain beneficiaries and excluding them avoids penalizing participants or distorting incentives. CMS will publish complete lists of excluded HCPCS codes and the methodology on the CJR-X web page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded Items and Services — Part B high-cost and low-volume drugs (performance-year criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: For episodes initiated during a performance year, in addition to baseline exclusions, exclude Part B payments for drug/biologic HCPCS codes that: (a) were not included in the baseline and appear in 10 or fewer episodes in the performance year; (b) were not included in the baseline, appear in >10 episodes in the performance year, and have mean cost > $25,000 per episode in the performance year; (c) were not in baseline, appear in >10 episodes, have mean cost ≤ $25,000, and correspond to a drug/biologic that appears in the baseline period list but was assigned a new HCPCS code between baseline and performance year; and (d) HCPCS codes for new hemophilia clotting factors not in the baseline period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This performance-year methodology is designed to capture new high-cost or low-volume Part B items that emerge after the baseline period, to avoid unfairly attributing high, unpredictable costs to participants. CMS will share lists with participants around preliminary target price release and update after the performance year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology and Process for Updating Exclusion Lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete lists of proposed excluded MS-DRGs for readmissions and excluded HCPCS codes for Part B services furnished during episodes will be posted on the CMS CJR-X web page. The methodology to identify excluded items/services applies to all performance years; lists would be shared with participants around preliminary target price release and updated after the performance year concludes. Revisions (such as adding MS-DRGs not covered by the stated categories) would be initiated through notice-and-comment rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes transparency (web posting) and a formal rulemaking process for substantive revisions to the exclusion lists and methods. Seeks comment on proposed excluded services and updating process (§§ 512.625(c),(d),(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode Duration (90-day post-discharge episode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to end episodes 90 days after discharge from the anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure; day 1 of the 90-day post-acute portion is the date of the anchor procedure or the date of discharge from an anchor hospitalization. Payments that span beyond the episode duration would be prorated so only the portion attributable to care during the fixed episode duration is attributed to episode spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: 90-day period marked by significant post-acute care needs, potential complications, and intensive management; aligns with professional global payment periods. CJR Model's 90-day episode demonstrated savings while maintaining quality, but shorter episodes (e.g., 30 days tested in TEAM) have less spending variability and lower ACO overlap. CMS will evaluate optimal episode length through comparison with TEAM; seeks comment on maintaining 90-day length at § 512.630(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode Termination / Cancellation Criteria (including death and EUC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an episode begins it continues until the end of the defined period unless canceled for specific reasons: (1) beneficiary ceases to meet general inclusion criteria; (2) outpatient LEJR procedure followed by inpatient admission on same day or within 3 days—then outpatient episode would not initiate and inpatient hospitalization would be the anchor; (3) beneficiary dies at any point during the episode (anchor hospitalization, anchor procedure, or post-discharge period); (4) the CJR-X participant is subject to the Extreme and Uncontrollable Circumstances (EUC) policy; (5) beneficiary is in the 30-day post-discharge period following a TEAM anchor hospitalization or procedure when they have a LEJR at a CJR-X participant hospital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an episode is canceled, services continue to be paid by Medicare as usual but there would be no episode spending reconciliation against the target price. Rationale for canceling on death: holding participants responsible for death during a 90-day episode would create too much uncertainty/variability. EUC policy proposed to apply only when (1) a major disaster declared under the Stafford Act and (2) section 1135 waivers issued for the county containing the participant's CCN address; CMS considered other identifiers (NPI/TIN) but proposes to continue using CCN address unless changed via rulemaking. CMS would cancel episodes initiated during an emergency period or in the 30 days before the start date of an emergency period as defined in 1135(g). CMS may consider future policies addressing cybersecurity via rulemaking. CMS seeks comment on proposed cancellation policy at § 512.630(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking Quality to Payment; Composite Quality Score (CQS) and scoring approach
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X would continue to link quality and payment to incentivize improvement. Proposed measures form a composite quality score (CQS) used to adjust the discount factor applied to participants' reconciliation target price during reconciliation. The measure set is a natural outgrowth of the CJR Model, maintaining focus on patient safety, patient experience, and health outcomes, with two notable variations: (1) greater weighting of the THA/TKA PRO; (2) addition of HOQR measures to account for outpatient LEJR procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS expects the CQS will sustain improvement across the care journey and incentivize hospitals to coordinate care across settings. The measures would be used to monitor performance and may be adjusted in future performance years through rulemaking. CMS seeks comment on additional measures for CJR-X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital-level Risk-Standardized Complication Rate (RSCR) following elective primary THA/TKA (CMIT ID #350)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use hospital-level RSCR following elective primary THA and/or TKA to assess episode quality performance starting in PY1. The THA/TKA Complications measure captures a hospital's rate of mortality, AMI, pneumonia, sepsis, pulmonary embolism, bleeding, infection, and mechanical failure following inpatient surgery. The outcome is defined as any one of the specified complications (not present on admission) occurring from date of admission to 90 days following admission; complications are counted only if they occur during the index admission or during a readmission. The complication outcome is dichotomous (yes/no): if a patient experiences ≥1 specified complications in the time period, the patient's outcome is a "yes." Specific time windows: AMI/pneumonia/sepsis during index admission or within 7 days of start of admission; surgical site bleeding/other surgical site complication/pulmonary embolism/death during index admission or within 30 days; mechanical complication/periprosthetic joint infection/wound complication during index admission or within 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: outcome measurement provides a broad view of quality, accounts for complex aspects of care, and is risk-standardized to reduce incentive to avoid higher-risk patients. Measure is actionable via preoperative optimization, perioperative protocol standardization, post-acute coordination, and early complication management. CMS proposes use at § 512.635(a)(1) and seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Visits Within 7 Days of Hospital Outpatient Department (HOPD) Surgery (CMIT ID #344, OP-36)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Hospital Visits within 7 days of HOPD Surgery measure to assess outpatient episode quality performance starting in PY1. The measure outcome is any of: (1) an inpatient admission directly after the surgery; or (2) an unplanned hospital visit (inpatient admission, observation stay, or emergency department visit) occurring after discharge or within 7 days of the surgery. The measure score is a ratio of predicted to expected number of post-surgical hospital visits among the HOPD's patients (denominator = expected visits given case mix and procedure mix; numerator = predicted number accounting for observed rate and volume). A score < 1 indicates fewer visits than expected; > 1 indicates more visits than expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: captures early, potentially preventable hospital utilization after outpatient same-day surgery (e.g., uncontrolled pain, urinary retention, infection, bleeding, VTE), complements the inpatient RSCR measure, reflects current clinical practice with high outpatient volume for LEJR, and is actionable for hospitals to improve discharge planning and post-op support. CMS proposes use at § 512.635(a)(2) and seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems Survey (HCAHPS) (CMIT ID #338)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include HCAHPS, the national standardized, publicly-reported survey instrument and data collection methodology measuring patients' perceptions of their hospital experience, as part of the CJR-X measure set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HCAHPS allows comparisons across hospitals and fosters incentives to improve quality through public reporting and transparency. It was used in the CJR Model and continues to inform patient experience measurement under CJR-X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outpatient and Ambulatory Surgery Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems Survey (OAS CAHPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include OAS CAHPS as a proposed measure to capture patient experience for outpatient same-day surgeries and to supplement inpatient patient-experience measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: high and growing proportion of LEJR procedures occur in outpatient settings; OAS CAHPS helps ensure quality accountability reflects outpatient clinical practice. CMS mentioned inclusion in the proposed measure set and seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital-Level THA/TKA Patient-Reported Outcome (PRO)-Based Performance Measure (PRO-PM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Hospital-Level THA/TKA PRO-PM (patient-reported outcomes) to assess outcomes from the patient's perspective; CMS proposes to weight this measure more heavily in the CQS. CJR-X would use THA/TKA PRO-PM data submitted to the HIQR for scoring model performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: PROs capture health status and multiple domains (physical, emotional, social) directly from patients, and provide valuable insights into how care affects patients' well-being. The HIQR now includes a THA/TKA PRO-PM developed from CJR Model voluntary submissions; CMS is committed to increased use of PROs and proposes higher weighting to incentivize patient-centered outcome measurement.
